result.rule: When the description states an activity together with a purpose, object, or scope that distinguishes what is being done: Label the corresponding BPMN task with its core action and enough of those stated details to preserve the activity’s meaning; do not add unsupported details or omit details that distinguish it.

When the description gives an activity together with contextual or implementation details: label the corresponding BPMN element with its core action and object, omitting details that do not distinguish the activity.

When the description identifies the object or information entity acted on by an activity: Label the corresponding BPMN activity using that stated entity rather than substituting a related but distinct one.
When the description states how the process begins or ends: Label the corresponding start and end events with the described trigger or outcome rather than generic labels.

Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
